findings.title: Claim allocation can consume an invocation and return a running claim after its absolute budgets expire
findings.contract: docs/async-plan.md cumulative lifetime and claim authority; rm305-independent-contract-review cumulative retry/lifetime accounting gate
findings.description: The sole database-time snapshot is taken before readLedger, FIFO, first-ledger insertion/readback and allocation. All budget comparisons and newly issued deadlines reuse that snapshot. The allocation UPDATE checks only fence exhaustion, not current database time, lifetime or invocation eligibility, and there is no post-allocation/state time check before returning a handle. A slow statement or awaited continuation can therefore pass the old budget check and commit running with an already-expired claim, including a reclaim after the immutable logical lifetime elapsed. The checked-in exhaustion tests expire records before entry, not during allocation.
findings.reproduction: Evaluate the unmodified production claim/outbox includes with Bun.Transpiler against SQLite :memory: inside real BEGIN/COMMIT. Delay only the allocation SQL callback before execution. First claim: lifetime/execution/lease 30ms, allocation delay 70ms. Reclaim: initial lifetime 100ms, execution 50ms, lease 20ms; expire the lease explicitly, then delay reclaim allocation 130ms.
findings.impact: Finite execution/lifetime admission is not currently guaranteed by the returned claim. An expired invocation is charged and the intent remains running until another claim evaluates fresh time, temporarily retaining the FIFO key. The independently tested dispatch checkpoint does reject the expired handle, so this finding is not evidence of a duplicate send or a bypass of possible-dispatch safety. The same snapshot/control-flow gap is shared by both adapter branches; PostgreSQL slow allocation was not independently executed here.
findings.requestedCorrection: Make allocation eligibility and handle admission depend on fresh authoritative database time, including a statement that itself finishes late. Never return a live-claim result after lease/execution/lifetime expiry; preserve absolute first-claim lifetime, cumulative accounting, fencing and possible-dispatch unknown conservatism. Add generated-host first-claim and reclaim tests delaying the allocation path across expiry, not just the checkpoint path. Any counter treatment for a late allocation must remain conservative and must not reset durable budgets.

positiveAssessments: The per-job/key write lock is acquired before current intent, ledger, FIFO and state decisions and is held through the caller transaction. With the compiler-owned schema and supported transaction isolation, it serializes competing claims/checkpoints/enqueues. Earlier pending/running/retry_wait/outcome_unknown intents block later same-key claims.

A running expired claim with possible_dispatch=1 transitions to outcome_unknown before any no-effect exhaustion/reclaim branch. It is not automatically resent or marked failed, and later same-key intents remain blocked. Pre-dispatch reclaim advances the database BIGINT fence and cumulative invocation count without resetting firstClaimAt or lifetimeDeadline.

Fence and key sequence values are cast to text at the boundary; arithmetic and FIFO comparison stay in SQL. The allocation overflow predicate fails closed rather than wrapping. The generated-host test covers a fence of 9007199254740993 and FIFO values above 2^53.

Checkpoint compares the stored claim ID and exact generation, checks possible_dispatch=0 and all three deadlines, then includes current database-time predicates in the UPDATE. Its post-statement database time rejects a late result while retaining a conservative marker. Rollback of the caller transaction also rolls back the checkpoint.

Finite positive safe integer limits are validated, invocation limit is capped at the database integer range, lease is constrained by execution, and existing ledger limits must match. Future compiler bindings must supply stable compiler-owned limits; arbitrary mutable/accessor host inputs are not an authored-authority approval.

The original outbox lifetime guard is preserved and the new claim/checkpoint executor is bound through it. Independent suspension probes rejected every tested post-revocation SQL invocation, including allocation, state updates and checkpoints.

retainedLimits: Private host-storage slice only. No authored/public/operator/worker binding, compiler-derived source/job identity or typed handler/version authority is certified.

No renewal, receipt/acknowledgement, cancellation transitions, no-effect retry scheduling, scheduler, dead-letter, attempt history or durable resolution implementation is certified. The 18-case ASYNC catalog and whole RM-306 remain incomplete.

Claims/checkpoints must be awaited inside their owning transaction. A positive checkpoint result is provisional inside that transaction, not permission to call a provider before commit acknowledgement. Future worker binding must handle commit uncertainty, delays through commit and dispatch, revalidation, cooperative cancellation and monotonic execution deadlines. Database fencing is not exactly-once external effect delivery.

The token prevents new guarded SQL invocation after revocation; it does not cancel an already-invoked statement, drain detached work or guard every unrelated persistence method. Nested transaction and detached/concurrent host-operation limitations from the prior correction review remain.

Lazy CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does not attest an existing schema or supply migrations. Root/claim access before required schema creation, missing backend, incompatible/corrupt/restored records, missing keys/foreign-key enforcement and malformed stored time still require their owning backend/schema guarantees. No schema collision/repair approval.

UUID collision handling, payload size/depth, absolute clock regressions/distributed clock accuracy, default clock/timeout/lease values and golden numeric limits are not newly approved. Database UTC is authority time, not a host-clock synchronization or hard active-query interruption guarantee.
The full-file hashes cover shared dirty files as observed, not unrelated retry/compiler semantics or later edits. Main's broad verification was not run or taken over by this reviewer.
